title: Mobile Collector Application

reconnaissance_findings.real_backend_is_not_ai_device_ai: Collector app talks to backend/ (Express+Prisma), not intelligence/device_ai (Python AI microservice used by P6.1/P6.2)
reconnaissance_findings.workflow_is_pickup_logistics_not_ai_capt: Submission model is a consumer-created waste pickup request (category/weight/address/geo/images), not an AI-detected device candidate; collector accepts/starts/completes it
reconnaissance_findings.no_self_service_collector_registration: POST /auth/register hard-codes UserRole.CONSUMER (backend/src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts); no role param in registerSchema
reconnaissance_findings.get_submission_by_id_is_owner_admin_only: loadAccessible() in submission.service.ts 404s for a collector fetching a pickup assigned to (not owned by) them; app resolves details from local cache instead
reconnaissance_findings.no_collector_history_endpoint: findByCollector query exists in submission.repository.ts but is never called by the service or wired to a route; only GET /collector/submissions (active assignments) is exposed

architecture.state_management: flutter_riverpod 3.4.2 (Notifier/NotifierProvider — StateNotifier/StateNotifierProvider were removed in this version, discovered via flutter analyze)
architecture.networking: dio, wrapped in ApiClient (Bearer + X-Request-ID) and mapDioExceptionToFailure (backend {success:false,error:{code,message}} envelope)
architecture.offline_storage: sqflite: sync_queue (queued actions) + submission_cache (last-known submission state)

screens.register: not implemented — backend has no self-service collector registration; honest info dialog instead
screens.device_capture_registration: not implemented — no such backend flow for collectors (real workflow is pickup accept/start/complete)
screens.submission_history: implemented — cache-backed, not server-backed (no history endpoint exists)

offline_sync_design.dedup: SyncQueueRepository.enqueue collapses re-taps of the same (submissionId, actionPath) into one row
offline_sync_design.reconciliation: SyncManager re-fetches submission status on a 4xx replay failure and treats the action as already-applied (drops from queue) if status shows it took effect, instead of endlessly retrying or duplicating
offline_sync_design.no_blind_retry: performOrQueue attempts once online; queues rather than looping on a retryable failure

environment.choco_install_attempt: failed — no admin rights (lib-bad directory access denied)
environment.direct_download_attempt: succeeded — Flutter 3.47.2 stable, ~1.93GB, downloaded to a user-writable directory, zip integrity verified before extraction
environment.riverpod_api_break_found: flutter_riverpod 3.4.2 removed StateNotifier/StateNotifierProvider; code rewritten against the actual installed package source (Notifier/NotifierProvider)

test_metrics.flutter_pub_get: resolved cleanly, all pinned versions valid
test_metrics.sqlite_test_note: sqflite_common_ffi ran against a real in-memory SQLite database — the native sqlite3 library is available in this environment
test_metrics.apk_build_reason: no Android SDK in this environment (flutter doctor: 'Unable to locate Android SDK'); Windows/web build targets available but not exercised (marginal additional verification value vs. platform-plugin-compatibility risk for platforms this app doesn't target)

security: Tokens only in flutter_secure_storage (Keystore/Keychain), never logged
No self-service creation of privileged (COLLECTOR) accounts possible
Client-side input validation in addition to server-side validation
Backend remains authoritative for every lifecycle transition — app never fabricates status locally
limitations: No self-service collector registration (backend design, not an app gap)
Submission History is cache-only, not a complete server-side history (no such endpoint exists)
Camera/scanner service abstractions implemented but not wired to a live flow (no backend endpoint to receive photos from a collector)
No push notifications for new assignments
Windows/web build targets untested (app targets Android/iOS; some plugins have partial/no desktop-web support)
